question: How does stock code on this firmware put a CJK-capable font on an LVGL v8 label?
prototype_hypothesis: The font comes from lvx_font_create(family, size, weight); labels get it as local style property 90 through the object's local-style setter.
callsite_evidence: 0xc2665f0 the body logs lvx_font_create_core / lvx_font_create from ext/lvx_font_manager.c and walks the family table at *(0x200bfc6c+548); unknown families fall back to LV_FONT_DEFAULT.

0xc23afe2 is the generic local-style setter: it fetches the style for the selector, stores (property, value) and marks the object for refresh. The v8 page-title creator applies its label font through the same family of calls.

A Manager page built on the 3.1.32 generation does not render: the first label create/refresh never returns and the watch restarts, consistent with LVGL's NULL-font path (the image carries the 'dsc->font == NULL' and 'Invalid font descriptor' strings).
control_flow_evidence: lvx_font_create(name, size, weight) -> family table lookup -> lv_font_t*.
local_style_set(label, 90, font, 0) -> the label's text font.
ownership_analysis: No ownership claimed. The created font is owned by the firmware font manager; the Manager only reads it.
unsafe_assumptions: MiSans-Regular is the family stock code uses for body text (it is the fallback name in the font manager).
Property 90 is the text-font property on this generation, by analogy with the audited 3.1.28 firmware; this is what the next device run checks.
Static evidence only; no device run has exercised these two entries yet.
recommended_probe: Rebuild the Supervisor, open the Manager page on Mirage and confirm the page renders instead of restarting the watch.
